title: How do you add keys for several outside providers, and choose a model for each kind of job?
lead: Should the hub's settings panel take a key for each outside provider, and let you pick which provider and model answers each kind of job (short questions, long drafts, pictures)? I recommend it: you set it once, agents still just ask for a draft or a picture, and the hub picks the model.
for_you: The Whole hub panel gets a key box per provider (Google, OpenAI, OpenRouter; Ollama needs none), like the Claude key box on the Account card
Under it, one line per job type: short questions, long drafts, pictures, each with its provider and model
Agents never choose a provider, model or address; the per-project switch and the spending caps stay as they are

for_you.text: Later, at your PC: paste your OpenRouter key into its box once

context: Matt (2026-11-17), after the first live picture test (Google, nano-banana 2.1, about $0.045): he wants a way to enter more than one provider's key, and picked per-job routing (option B in chat) to build in from the start. He has just opened an OpenRouter account. Today (decision 80, PR #145 merged): one provider and model answer for the whole hub, and a key can be saved only by running the live-check script in PowerShell, so the hub panel shows Google as the provider even before anything is saved. Typing a key into the page has precedent: the Account card already takes the Anthropic API key (decision 78), kept with the same Windows per-user protection. OpenRouter alone reaches hundreds of models (Mistral, DeepSeek, Grok, Llama, Qwen and others), so direct boxes for those providers can wait; each one that speaks the same request format needs only its address and prices. Pictures through OpenRouter are untested; only Google is tested live.

options.name: Key per provider, model per job type
options.summary: Key boxes for each provider in the Whole hub panel (saved protected, page sees the last four only), plus a provider and model chosen for each job type: short questions, long drafts, pictures. The live-check script stays as a test tool.
pros: Cheapest suitable model for each job, set once
No PowerShell step to add a key
Agents' tools and the caps don't change
cons: A few more settings on the panel
Keys now typed into the page, so the save path needs a careful review
options.effort: Medium (one implementer, then a deep review of the key handling)
options.source: Claude's judgment; Matt leaned this way in chat

options.name: Key per provider, still one provider at a time
options.summary: Key boxes for each provider in the panel, but one provider and model still answer every job; you switch by hand.
cons: Switching to OpenRouter for text would drop Google for pictures
Per-job choice would have to be added later anyway

options.name: Per-job choice, keys still by script
options.summary: Add the per-job provider and model lines, but keys keep being saved only with the PowerShell live-check script.
pros: Keys never pass through the page
cons: A PowerShell step for every new key, and not from the phone

recommendation: A: key boxes per provider and a provider and model per job type, with the panel showing plainly when a key or a choice isn't saved yet.
change_mind: If keys in the page feel like too much exposure, take C and keep adding keys with the script.

settles.value: the hub picks provider and model per job type (short question, long draft, picture), set by the human in hub settings; agents never choose; keys entered in hub settings, DPAPI-protected per user, page sees the last four only
